WHO CAN REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? A person subject to the Code of Ethics may request an advisory opinion about a particular provision of the Code which may affect him or her. WHEN SHOULD I REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? If you believe you may face a real or potential conflict of interest, the time to request an advisory opinion is before you take any official action.

HOW DO I REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? To request an advisory opinion, you must either mail or hand-deliver to the Commission a letter containing your original signature and the following information: • Your name, official position, and a description of your duties; • Your daytime telephone number and e-mail address; • Briefly, the name, jurisdiction and powers of your agency, commission, or office; • The nature of the potential conflict; • A summary of relevant facts; and • Any time constraints.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER I SUBMIT MY REQUEST? ► Letter confirming receipt ► Draft recommendation prepared by staff attorney ► You are strongly encouraged to attend hearing ► Affirmative vote of 5 of 9 Commissioners required ► You will receive written copy ► Also available on Ethics Commission website ► Advisory Opinion and request are public records

Who is required to file? ► All state and municipal elected officials ► Candidates for state or municipal elected office ► All state and some municipal appointed officials ► Some public employees who hold major decision- making positions
All officials required to file must continue to file Financial Disclosure Statements until they have been out of office for one full calendar year.
When must the statement be filed? The Code of Ethics requires that a Financial Disclosure Statement be filed with the Ethics Commission by the last Friday in April . . .
or . . . within (30) days of: ► appointment to a public position; ► the deadline for filing candidacy for public office; or ► the filing of a Notice of Organization with the Board of Elections.

What is the purpose of financial disclosure? ► helps ensure that those people who are acting in the public interest do not use their public positions to further their private financial interests ► provides evidence that there are no conflicts between an official’s financial interests and his or her public office

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Bill #2026-2027-01 October 15, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting - FOR ACTION (Introduced at the September 17, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting) Creates standard process for committee formation Approved by FSEC 08/31/26 and 10/7/26 (as amended) Reviewed by CBUM 09/28/26 and 10/8/26 (as amended) Legislation effective date: Spring semester 2027 Rationale: The limited number of faculty senators, in combination with University-Manual-mandated committee staffing requirements, can make it difficult to staff an expanding number of standing committees.
This makes it important to ensure that additional standing committees and subcommittees, whose charges and memberships are proscribed in the University Manual, are created only in response to a significant and sustained need.
In contrast, special committees can be created by the Faculty Senate to address pressing issues.
While there is no limit to the length of time a special committee can exist, the faculty senate must vote to reauthorize each special committee each year.

This legislation mandates that a newly formed committee must exist as a special committee for at least three (3) years before legislation reconstituting it as a standing committee or subcommittee can be considered by the Faculty Senate.
Such legislation must be accompanied by language specifying the charge and membership of the standing committee for inclusion in the University Manual.
This change provides time for the Faculty Senate to 1) consider whether a new standing committee or subcommittee is truly warranted; and 2) craft an appropriate and achievable charge for the body.
This legislation does not mandate that a special committee must be reconstituted as a standing committee after three years.
It is also not retroactive, i.e., all existing standing committees and subcommittees remain unchanged.
This original version of this legislation was introduced for discussion at the 9/17/26 Faculty Senate meeting.
The final version has been revised as follows in response to faculty/staff comments. 1.
Remove language mentioning joint committees .
Joint committees are, by definition, created in concert with the administration (staffing, wording, charge, power balance).

While the faculty and administration may choose to designate a joint committee as a special joint committee subject to the rules and procedures detailed below, the power to do so does not rest exclusively with the faculty senate. 2.
Identify the assessment process and who conducts it.
Added language to §4.12.1 specifying that the Special Committee’s self-assessment shall be reviewed by FSEC.
FSEC which shall use it as the basis for a recommendation to the Faculty Senate to vote on whether the 1

Committee should dissolve, continue as a Special Committee, or be reconstituted as a permanent Standing Committee or Subcommittee. 3.
What happens if no reauthorization vote is taken before the end of the AY?
Added language to §4.11.1 specifying that all Special Committees are annually authorized by vote of the Faculty Senate.
A Special Committee that has not received an affirmative reauthorization vote (assuming that no duly authorized extension has been granted) within one year of authorization shall be dissolved. 4.
After the third-year review, can a reauthorized Special Committee apply to change its status?
Added language to §4.12.1 specifying that a Special Committee must wait at least two years after its third-year review (i.e., be in its fifth consecutive year of operation) before requesting that the Faculty Senate reconsider reconstituting it as a Standing Committee or Subcommittee.

Capital Improvement Plan FY22‐FY26 Presentation to the Finance and Facilities Committee October 23, 2020

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically on July 1st. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? There are 5 levels of approval. They are: 1. University of Rhode Island ‐ Facilities Committee (April & May) 2. University of Rhode Island ‐ Senior Leadership (May & June) 3. University of Rhode Island ‐ Board of Trustees (June) 4. Executive Branch 1. Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July‐December) 2. Final Approval by Governor’s Office (Third week of January) 5. Legislative Branch 1. Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) 2. Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and, total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 25% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.

COURSE REPORT Special Summer Curriculum Committee Report 2026-2027-SSCC-01-A At the July 14, 2026 meeting of the Special Summer Curriculum Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate Executive Committee for approval. informational matters TEMPORARY COURSE BPS346X: Self-Paced Skills Laboratory for Pharmaceutical Scientists, Fall 2026 (2 crs.) Explores core experimental techniques used in biomedical and pharmaceutical research.
Supports students before or during independent research, and emphasizes practical skill development, quantitative reasoning, and the connection between experimental data and biological or pharmacological questions.
Students will learn how to design assays, generate and analyze data, and evaluate experimental results with an emphasis on accuracy, reproducibility, and good laboratory practice.
Students will select specialized experimental modules aligned with their research interests or future laboratory placements.

By the end of the course, students will work more independently and effectively in biomedical or pharmaceutical research laboratories, with a strong foundation in experimental technique, data analysis, and scientific communication. (Lab. 3) Pre: BPS345 and permission by the chair of BPS. for confirmation by the senate NEW COURSES BPS493: Scholars in Biomedical & Pharmaceutical Sciences, Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Student forum to present research projects, discuss experimental design and results, and engage in scientific dialogue with peers and faculty.
Research topics may span areas such as drug discovery, pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutics, pharmacokinetics, environmental health, and natural products.
Through structured presentations and discussion, students develop skills in scientific communication, data interpretation, and critical evaluation of research.
Exposes participants to diverse research approaches within pharmaceutical sciences, helping students connect laboratory research with concepts

learned in the classroom.
Students will strengthen their ability to present scientific work professionally, ask thoughtful questions, and engage in scholarly discussion—skills essential for graduate study, professional programs, and careers in biomedical research. (Seminar) Pre: BPS194, BPS250, credit or concurrent enrollment in BPS345.
May be repeated for a maximum of 4 credits.
S/U only for students not concurrently enrolled in an independent study.

Not for graduate credit.
CSC465: Fundamentals of Machine Learning Security, Fall 2026 (4 crs.) Fundamentals of the security of artificial intelligence and machine learning systems. (Lec. 4) Pre: MTH141 and CSC310, or by permission of instructor.

President DATE: June 10, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of Contracts in Excess of $5 Million Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board o olicy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of one new contract for HVAC repair services, and three change orders for existing contracts with Performance Food Group and First Transit.
Recommendation: I recommend approval of the new contract and three change orders as presented.
Each contract represents ongoing support services which are part of the current operations of the campus.
Points to Consider: A new contract in support of HVAC Maintenance and Repair.
The solicitation and award of a renewal contract for HVAC Maintenance and Repair is ongoing through the RI Division of Purchases.
This will be a three (3) year contract based on time and material rates.

The control value (not to exceed) has been calculated at $7.6 million.
This amount is in line with prior spend for a 3-year contract.
The lowest qualified bidder will be selected by the RI Division of Purchases, but -June.
The contract is expected to begin on 07/01/24.
A change order to contract with First Transit Inc. for campus shuttle services.
This contract was in place prior to the execution of the policy indicated above.
It is a time and material contract based on usage throughout the year.
The current contract expires 06/30/25.
Based on current usage, we anticipate needing an additional $400,000 to be added to the current Purchase Order (PO) value of $9.2 million.
A change order to contract with Performance Food Group, Inc.
This contract is for a prime food vendor to supply groceries and sundries to URI Dining Services as needed.
The original award predated the above policy, but Board approval was obtained in April of 2023 via a change order.
The proposed increase of $7M to extend the contract for an additional year is in line with the annual usage and prior spend of this contract.
